title: SMART FINANCE MANAGEMENT SYSTEM BASED ON ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE TECHNOLOGIES
venue: Problems of applied mathematics and mathematical modeling
tldr: Presents an intelligent personal finance management system integrating supervised and unsupervised machine learning with LLMs for transaction classification, forecasting, anomaly detection, and personalized recommendations.
problem_and_motivation: Traditional budgeting methods are insufficient for achieving the desired accuracy and adaptability due to growing financial data complexity. There is a need for intelligent systems that automate financial record-keeping, analysis, and optimization.
approach: Implements k-NN and decision trees for transaction classification.
Uses ARIMA and LSTM models for expense forecasting.
Applies autoencoders, Isolation Forest, and SVM for anomaly detection.
Generates personalized recommendations using collaborative filtering, matrix factorization, and LLMs.
Connects to banking APIs via OAuth2 and supports CSV data imports.
Stores data in a PostgreSQL database for scalable and reliable storage.
Implements a two-level modular architecture with REST API for inter-module communication.
System is implemented in Python using libraries like pandas, scikit-learn, tensorflow, and openai.
Generates analytical visualizations and textual recommendations.
Utilizes a locally deployed AI module for generating insights.
findings: num: Classification accuracy of 91.2% was achieved using k-NN and decision trees.
num: Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) was 6.8% for ARIMA and 5.4% for LSTM.
num: F1-score for anomaly detection was 0.86 using autoencoders and Isolation Forest.
Combining statistical models with modern AI techniques enhances the performance of personal finance management systems.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: This paper contributes a comprehensive architecture for an AI-driven personal finance management system that integrates multiple machine learning paradigms. It provides a practical framework combining classical statistical methods, deep learning, and generative AI for automated financial analysis. The paper demonstrates the feasibility and performance of a hybrid system through empirical results on a sample dataset.
directly_justifies: Combining traditional statistical models with modern AI techniques enhances performance of personal finance management systems.
The Smart Wallet prototype achieved 91.2% classification accuracy and an F1-score of 0.86 for anomaly detection.
LSTM outperformed ARIMA with a MAPE of 5.4% compared to 6.8%.
limits: The experimental dataset is limited to 1000 transactions, which may not represent real-world scale and diversity.
The paper does not detail the composition of the dataset or its representativeness, limiting generalizability.
topic_relevance.topic_mapping_rationale: A systematic scan across all topic domains revealed direct relevance to expense categorization, predictive modeling, anomaly detection, and budget recommendation. The paper's core contributions center on algorithmic methods for transaction classification (3.A), forecasting (6.A, 6.B), and anomaly detection (8.A, 8.B), with a clear application to budget recommendation (7.B). Topic 7.A was assigned medium relevance as budgeting strategies are implied but not formally defined. Evaluation topics (12.A, 12.B) were marked medium because the paper reports performance metrics but lacks a rigorous comparative evaluation. Domains related to culturally specific practices (2.A, 2.B), demographic specifics (1.A-C), mobile design (9.A-C), privacy (10.A-C), and engagement (11.A-B) were considered but rejected as the paper provides no content on these subjects, focusing instead on algorithmic architecture and initial performance validation.

limitations: The dataset used for testing is limited to 1000 transactions. [unacknowledged]
